ADR-01.title: Equivalence Architecture
consumed_contracts: total effects remain an exact raw computation layer

decision.statement: Use Mathlib Finmap as the authoritative finite dependent flat store; use Set K for semantic specifications and Finset K for executable specifications and provisions; separate total raw store operations from legal binding transitions with guarded partial inverses; use proof-indexed success views, Option mathematical partiality, and Except diagnostics connected by refinement; add an outcome-dependent Option-Kleisli partial-effect companion to ADR-01; and represent D24 operations by typed per-key codes with key-local lifts.

global_assumptions.reason: presence and finite-key computation compare keys, not service values; Finmap carries finite support without making the entire key type finite

store.name: dependent-function-plus-finite-support-proof
store.reason: It does not directly carry executable support enumeration and recreates Finmap; it remains an allowed semantic view.

store.name: mathlib-finmap
store.reason: It is a finite dependent map with dependent lookup, keys, insert, erase, extract, union, and extensionality.

store.name: dfinsupp
store.reason: It requires zero/default values and would conflate absence with zero.

store.name: finsupp-to-sigma-values
store.reason: It loses the key-indexed value-type invariant and requires casts or validation.

store.name: custom-carrier-polymorphic-store-class
store.reason: The stable proof-facing facade is fixed, but a higher-kinded abstraction has no demonstrated second implementation yet.

specification.name: set-only
specification.reason: Arbitrary predicates are not generally enumerable or decidable.

specification.name: finset-only
specification.reason: It silently strengthens every semantic statement to finite specifications.

specification.name: set-finite-proof-as-runtime-data
specification.reason: A propositional finiteness proof is not the executable finite enumeration consumed by notify.

specification.name: set-and-finset-with-adequacy
specification.reason: It retains semantic generality and executable enumeration with an explicit bridge.

partiality.name: proof-arguments-only
partiality.reason: It cannot execute unchecked runtime input or model common-domain partiality.

partiality.name: option-only
partiality.reason: It is the correct mathematical erasure but insufficient for runtime diagnostics.

partiality.name: except-only
partiality.reason: It makes diagnostic payload comparison infect operation law and independence theorems.

partiality.name: failure-totalized-as-identity
partiality.reason: It invents a false transition and weakens protocol and recovery semantics.

partiality.name: proof-success-plus-option-semantics-plus-except-diagnostics
partiality.reason: Each interface has one role and erasure/refinement theorems prevent semantic drift.

adr01_bridge.name: force-partial-operations-into-total-effect
adr01_bridge.reason: It erases preconditions and definedness or hides them behind artificial defaults.

adr01_bridge.name: independent-duplicated-partial-theory
adr01_bridge.reason: It duplicates ADR-01 result relations, inverse laws, and specializations.

adr01_bridge.name: option-kleisli-companion-with-total-embedding
adr01_bridge.reason: It makes partial composition honest and proves the total ADR-01 fragment is a specialization.

affected_disposition_nodes.effective_readiness_rule: remove only BD-COEFFECT from each node blocker set; preserve all other blockers and all frozen dependency edges

coding_rules: Use the Store facade and do not unfold Finmap entries downstream.
Require DecidableEq K only at executable boundaries and do not assume Fintype K globally.
Do not require value equality for presence, satisfaction, recovery, or observation.
Keep Set semantic specifications and Finset executable specifications distinct and bridged.
Never infer arbitrary Set satisfaction decidability from finite store support.
Keep raw overwrite and erase-no-op functions separate from legal protocol transitions.
An invalid protocol operation has no successor and is never identity.
Use Option for mathematical partiality and Except for diagnostics with erasure theorems.
Compose partial functions with Option bind and never with defaults.
Compose partial effects with outcome-dependent bind; second-stage failure has no big-step successor and successful inverses compose in reverse order.
Before restricting a partial operation to a total ADR-01 effect, prove forward totality, successor invariant closure, returned-undo totality on the invariant, and undo-result invariant closure.
Preserve definedness, successor relation, selected inverse, inverse properness, recovery, and exact outcomes.
Use typed operation codes for heterogeneous D24, D34, and D41 syntax.
Separate domain-preserving D24 operations from domain-changing binding transitions.
Returned binding inverses re-check protocol presence or absence and never use unchecked overwrite as the inverse semantics.
Scope T40 to distinct flat physical keys.
Aggregate tables of exactly Active fibers only, under finite-registry and registered-provision disjointness invariants.
Name registered possible providers, active providers, and present bindings separately.
State D69 only over successful completed activations.
